explanation: erdosproblems.com/652: Mathialagan [Ma21] proved that for a set P of k points and a set Q of n points with 2 ≤ k ≤ n^{1/3}, some point of P determines ≫ (kn)^{1/2} distances to points of Q. The Lean statement: ∃ c > 0 such that for finite P, Q ⊆ ℝ² with |P| ≥ 2 and |P|³ ≤ |Q|, some p ∈ P has |{dist(p,q) : q ∈ Q}| ≥ c√(|P||Q|). Counting a possible zero distance (p ∈ Q) only weakens the claim by 1. (The docstring cites Theorem 14; the forum thread refers to Theorem 3.6 of the same paper — a citation detail only.) Faithful.
